//: STANDARD OPERATING SETTINGS — the federation-owned shared FLOOR for every Architect's .claude/settings.json. GENERATED consumers: curate/gen-settings.py stamps this floor + a system's own `settings_extras` (from its session.config.json) into that system's .claude/settings.json, which is a GENERATED do-not-hand-edit file. Per ADR-0034 (settings are federation-pushed substrate). This file is the single source of the floor; a system adds — never subtracts — via settings_extras. Substrate enforcement of ADR-0012/ADR-0007 (blanket maintenance authority over one's own repo) and P9/P10 (destructive ops gated; routine ops architect-owned). Genuinely per-machine overrides live in the gitignored settings.local.json.
//hooks: SHARED floor hooks. SessionStart (matcher 'startup' ONLY) runs TWO commands that — like all Claude Code hooks — execute IN PARALLEL with no ordering guarantee: (1) session.py start — the mechanical session-start ritual (git-state diagnosis, machine detect, time, next-session number, evidence-based orphan triage, write the start stamp) per ADR-0020/ADR-0035, injecting CANON.md + STANDARD.md + the prior handoff entry + user profile as additionalContext per ADR-0022/ADR-0024/ADR-0035, and STAGING the user-visible banner into a per-session file keyed by the stdin session_id; (2) session.py announce — POLLS for that per-session file (bounded, fail-open) and prints the banner (start stamp + any just-auto-closed orphan's end stamp) to plain stdout, the one SessionStart channel that renders to the user, since hookSpecificOutput.systemMessage is upstream-broken (#9090/#50542). announce must POLL, not assume start already ran: they race. Keying the file by session_id makes a stale prior-session banner impossible (the v2.21.0 shared-announce.txt bug, session 59). Split into two hooks so start's own stdout stays pure JSON. A THIRD startup hook, standard_check.py --status (ADR-0047), runs the member's LOCAL standard-version self-check (read-only, fail-open) and prints a one-line signal to stdout — the ring-1 self-check the federation's fleet reconciliation (curate/standard_version.py) mirrors fleet-wide. A FOURTH startup hook, session.py apply-briefs (ADR-0039 Fork A, floor-promoted session 66), auto-adopts conforming Apply:auto briefs from the member's inbox (CFG['inbox']) before the model wakes and surfaces the rest — deterministic, whole-brief-atomic, never-commit (the session-end close commits, so a bad apply shows in git diff), fail-open, and a no-op when a member declares no inbox. The inbox is machine-local (proposed-edits/ is gitignored, delivered by copy: queued in outbox/, carried by origin and drained by each machine's mail poller per ADR-0107, with ADR-0027's copy-into-the-inbox semantics), so it does not race the start hook's git pull. This is the fleet-wide half of zero-touch adoption: every member with the shipped session.py auto-adopts, not just the federation. Both session.py hooks WRITE/read handoff state, so must not fire on resume/clear — hence the 'startup' matcher. The Stop, PreToolUse-heartbeat, and SessionEnd hooks maintain the ADR-0036 liveness sidecar (.session-state/, gitignored): Stop runs session.py heartbeat after every assistant turn, and an unmatchered (all-tools) PreToolUse entry runs the SAME command on every tool call (ADR-0054 — Stop fires only BETWEEN turns, so one long working turn made a live session look crashed and get falsely reaped; tool calls beat constantly DURING a turn; writes are throttled in-command to one per minute). SessionEnd runs session.py record-end to mark a clean exit (fires on clean termination but NOT on crash — the discriminator the next start's auto-triage uses). The FIRST heartbeat of a session also MATERIALIZES its lazy start (ADR-0055): the hook-path `start` defers all mutating work (journal write, handoff compile, reap, auto-push) behind a .pending-start marker, and the first beat — a signal a phantom SessionStart (the desktop-app pre-spawn class) never produces — completes it; phantoms are thereby no-ops by construction. All are fast + fail-open. Systems that run extra SessionStart probes (e.g. the federation's curate/reconcile status hooks) or their own PreToolUse guards add them via settings_extras.hooks (keyed by event), never here.
//worktreeremove: WorktreeRemove -> session.py worktree-remove: the TEARDOWN half of the ADR-0060 worktree-lane lifecycle, floor-promoted (from a federation-only settings_extra) so concurrency is a fleet capability rather than a federation privilege. Claude Code DELEGATES worktree removal to a configured hook and only falls back to `git worktree remove` when none exists, so this hook must do the removal itself — a hook that merely prunes leaves the lane dir AND its lock behind, and the still-checked-out branch then refuses `git branch -d`, stranding the branch and its coordination holds. Order is load-bearing: remove the worktree, prune admin entries, THEN `git branch -d` (merged-only — an unmerged lane never landed, so it is KEPT for `poga lanes --clean` with its work safe on the branch; P9, no work is ever destroyed) and release that lane's coord claims. Never --force: bare `remove` refuses a dirty lane, which is the outcome we want. FAIL-OPEN (always exit 0 — never block a session's exit). The LAUNCH half is the `poga` script, shipped byte-identical beside session.py; the LAND half is `session.py end` run inside the lane. A member missing this hook can still land a lane, but accumulates worktree dirs and merged branches until swept by hand — which is exactly the state the fleet was in before this promotion.
//pretooluse: Two PreToolUse STRUCTURAL GUARDS plus one unmatchered LIVENESS HEARTBEAT (session.py heartbeat on every tool call — not a guard, never denies; see //hooks and ADR-0054), all reading the hook JSON on stdin and FAILING OPEN on any error. (1) Bash -> session.py check-bash: DENIES (a) any DESTRUCTIVE git op (force/mirror/delete push, reset --hard/--keep, force branch delete, interactive/onto rebase, filter-branch/-repo, clean -f, update-ref -d, reflog expire, gc --prune) classified AFTER stripping `git -C <path>`/wrappers, so it catches the `git -C <repo> …` forms the prefix-anchored deny-list below cannot match (confirm-destructive-ops / P9) — this runs FIRST and UNCONDITIONALLY, checks every segment of a chain, and is never gated on config; (b) any FALSE-GREEN RUN (WI-0344) — a test suite (`pytest`, `python -m unittest|pytest`, `curate/run_suite.py`) or a land (`session.py merge`), or the honest verbs `session.py test` / `poga test`, with anything running AFTER it in the same command, so the exit status that comes back belongs to the downstream command and a failing run reports 0. Also unconditional, and for the same reason as (a): the motivation was never prompt-matching. `&&` is exempt (a non-zero left side short-circuits, so the failure survives), a run that is the LAST thing in the command is allowed however long the chain before it, and `--collect-only`/`--help`/`--version` have no verdict to lose. The deny names the sanctioned form — `python3 session.py test` run bare, which writes stdout and stderr to separate FILES and prints PASSED/FAILED/DID NOT REPORT. Eight recorded occurrences (WI-0139 sessions ~129/~134/~148 plus five found by WI-0344's journal sweep) against an honest verb that already existed are what moved this from prose into code; and (c) any top-level &&/||/;/|/newline compound ONLY where the system sets `compound_bash_guard: true` in session.config.json. (c) is RETIRED AND OFF BY DEFAULT per ADR-0087: its motivation was that allow-strings cannot match a compound command, which the harness's auto permission mode obsoleted, so the `no-compound-bash` habit is Deprecated and the code kept live behind the switch. Parser is quote/heredoc/command-substitution aware (a commit message containing ;/&& is allowed). NOTE (WI-0344): the parser now splits on `|` as well, so a pipeline's later stages are segments in their own right — `echo x | git -C <repo> reset --hard` is seen by (1a) where it was not before, and `git status | sh` no longer auto-approves at (1d). (1d) AFTER (1a)/(1b)/(1c) clear, check-bash AUTO-APPROVES the safe git surface (permissionDecision 'allow') — the read-only + forward-only verbs that mirror the floor's plain-git allow-list — so `git -C <path> <verb>` stops prompting (no allow-string can match it; see //git-c). A piped tail of inert readers (`head`, `tail`, `wc`, `grep`, …, none of which can write a file or run a program) keeps its fast path; anything else in a pipeline falls through to the prompt. Parity, not new trust: destructive git is denied at (1a) FIRST, and a hook 'allow' can't override a settings deny. (2) AskUserQuestion -> session.py check-question: the guard for P17 ask-in-prose-not-pickers — DENIES the multiple-choice picker so questions are asked in prose, not chip UI. ON BY DEFAULT; the one off switch (WI-0451) is `"interaction": {"pickers": "allow"}` in the system's own session.config.json, and a missing, malformed or unreadable value keeps the deny (fails closed). It does NOT affect harness permission prompts (a separate mechanism). Both enforce by substrate instead of self-discipline (P15 / add-structural-guard-on-recurrence).
//git-c: OUT-OF-TREE git (`git -C <path> <verb>`) CANNOT be matched by any permission allow-string: Claude Code's matcher parses the git command and the `-C /path` global option defeats the prefix match, so neither `Bash(git -C:*)` nor `Bash(git status:*)` ever fires for it (confirmed against the CC permission docs, session 60 — this is why exact-command `git -C …` allows kept piling up one-per-session in settings.local.json). The operative suppression is therefore NOT a settings string but the check-bash PreToolUse hook (see //pretooluse (1d)), which AUTO-APPROVES the safe git surface (permissionDecision 'allow'). The `Bash(git -C:*)` / `Bash(git -C *)` entries below are retained as a harmless documented fallback (they'd start working if CC ever fixes the matcher) but are inert today. SAFETY: the auto-approve is made safe by (a) check-bash denying destructive git FIRST, regardless of the `-C` prefix, and (b) CC's deny-first precedence — a hook 'allow' can never override a settings `deny`. Do NOT remove or disable the check-bash guard, or `git -C <path> push --force`/`reset --hard` become ungated. NOTE (ADR-0087): the `compound_bash_guard` config flag turns off ONLY the compound deny — it does not and must not gate this destructive-git check, which stays unconditional even when config is missing or malformed.

Notification.//: WI-0162 / ADR-0101: a lane waiting on the user writes an `attention` record into the coordination store, cleared by the next tool use and at session end. THE RECORD IS THE TRUTH; delivery is best-effort, because an interrupt that fails is silent by construction. Three states end to end — waiting / clear / CANNOT TELL — and unknown is never rendered as clear. Federation-only from 2026-08-22, promoted to the floor 2026-09-14 after its cycle.

//lane-verification-floor: WI-0292. `poga authorize check` and `poga authorize list` are the READ side of ADR-0112, and they sit in the FLOOR rather than in any one system's settings_extras because of what the read side is FOR. A grant exists so a DISPATCHED lane can cite a record instead of trusting a peer's prose — and a dispatched lane is a detached tmux TUI with default permission posture and NOBODY ATTACHED (sessionlib/lanes.py `_dispatch_spawn_command` passes no -p, no --permission-mode, no --allowedTools), so a command matching no allow entry does not run: it raises a prompt into a pane with no one to answer it. The verifier was therefore unrunnable in exactly the population the mechanism was built for. MEASURED 2026-09-05: lane poga-28 was handed G-47b435, could not run the check, correctly refused to proceed on an unverifiable grant, and the operator who minted it to unblock three lanes learned it had unblocked none an hour later. A mechanism whose verifier cannot run degrades to the thing it replaced. BOTH SPELLINGS ARE LISTED because they are one capability, not two: `poga authorize check` execs `python3 session.py authorize-check` as a CHILD process (poga:1029-1031), and a child is never permission-checked — only the spelling a lane TYPES is. Listing only the session.py form would teach members to go around the wrapper to get work done, which is how a wrapper stops being the path. WHY UNATTENDED IS SAFE HERE: both verbs are read-only by construction — `resolve_grant` opens the store WITHOUT create=True and writes nothing, `authorize-check` prints one sentence and exits 0 only on GRANTED and 1 on all five non-granted states — and per ADR-0112 D10 the grant store is not an access control, so reading it confers nothing. MINT and REVOKE are deliberately absent: those write, and minting is the operator's act, never a lane's. Nothing here is assumed any more — `poga authorize` probes its own effective allow-list at MINT time (sessionlib/config.py `grant_verifiability`) and stamps the answer on the grant, so an unverifiable grant is reported when it is ISSUED rather than discovered through a refusal an hour later.
